records.name: Bachelors Barge Club
records.summary: An adult rowing club on Boathouse Row. People new to rowing take a short run of learn to row lessons in gig boats, and the club takes members after an application.
records.what_you_do: Take about five or six gig lessons with a coach, then row gigs on your own. Move to team boats after roughly 50 miles in a gig, and later to a more advanced shell with coaching. Members pay dues.

cost.text: Dues apply; the amount was not shown on the pages read

first_step.how: Complete the application form on the membership page. Applicants must be over 18 and able to swim. Space is limited, so you may be put on a waiting list.
first_step.basis: Membership needs an application and may mean a waiting list before you see what the club is like.

records.notes: The home page shows a template street address, phone and email, so those are left out. The membership page gives a drexel.edu address for inquiries, which is recorded as published and not verified. Named as a full Schuylkill Navy member. No dated news on the site, so status rests on a working site.

records.name: Crescent Boat Club
records.summary: A Schuylkill Navy rowing club at #5 Boathouse Row that takes people with no rowing background and runs summer programs for novices and juniors.
records.what_you_do: Start with novice sculling or sweep rowing, or sign a junior up for the summer program. Members can move from first outings through masters racing.

schedule.text: Summer programs for novices and junior rowers. The newest dated program notice seen is from May 2025, and no 2026 dates are shown.

cost.text: Dues and youth fees are on the membership and youth pages, not on the home page

first_step.how: Send an inquiry through the form on the membership page. Youth program applications go through RegattaCentral.
first_step.basis: The club says no rowing experience is needed to join, and it takes people from their first outing on.

records.notes: No email or phone is published; all inquiries go through forms. Dated site news: 2025 summer rowing programs (May 2025), a 2025 board election (March), and older 2023 items.

records.name: Malta Boat Club

records.what_you_do: Row socially on the river, use the erg and weight space, meet in the club rooms, and get support if you race in Navy or city regattas.

records.what_you_do: Take an adult Learn to Row class, join a masters crew, or sign a junior or high school rower up for the junior pathway or the summer camp.

records.name: University Barge Club
records.summary: A Schuylkill Navy member club that offers recreational rowing on the Schuylkill and a masters team that races local regattas.
records.what_you_do: Row recreationally on the Schuylkill River, or train with the masters team for local regattas such as the Head of the Schuylkill and the Independence Day Regatta.

first_step.how: Use the Learn More page or the contact page. The site shows no sign-up steps, and the members area needs a login.

records.name: Vesper Boat Club
records.summary: A competitive rowing club at 10 Kelly Drive with masters racing crews, a post-collegiate racing team, and a three-month summer camp for rowers under 23. Its site posts race and club news through 2026.
records.what_you_do: Masters rowers train and race in local and national regattas. Post-collegiate sweep rowers join the racing team, which practices year round. Athletes under 23 can attend the summer camp.

first_step.how: Use the contact form on the club website. The page does not describe how to join.
first_step.basis: The site is built around competitive racing, and joining steps are not shown.

records.notes: Several September and October 2026 headlines repeat one title, so they were not used as evidence. The July 2026 item (a U23 team result at RowFest) is used. No email or phone is published, only a contact form. The Vesper home page lists a 2026 masters erg event in May.

records.name: Sedgeley Club
records.summary: A women's social club in the Turtle Rock lighthouse building on Kelly Drive. Members and guests gather for lunches, teas and dinners, and the clubhouse is rented out for meetings and parties.
records.what_you_do: Attend member lunches, teas and dinners, and the membership events listed on the contact page. The building is also cared for by Friends of Historic Sedgeley, a nonprofit that runs open houses.

first_step.how: Use the contact page for membership information. Upcoming membership events are listed there.
first_step.basis: The site says it welcomes new members, but it does not show how to apply or what dues cost.

Friends of Historic Sedgeley is listed in leads_only.

records.name: PA Center for Adapted Sports
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs year-round sport and wellness programs for people with disabilities from an office on Boathouse Row. Adapted rowing, indoor rowing and kayaking are among its 13 programs.
records.what_you_do: Take part in adapted rowing, indoor rowing or kayaking, or in other programs such as climbing or yoga. The site also has a volunteer page.

first_step.how: Read the eligibility document and use the contact page. The site does not describe the sign-up steps.
first_step.basis: Eligibility is checked through a linked document and no sign-up process is shown.

records.name: Dock and Community Boathouse at Bartram's Garden
records.summary: Free community boating on the Schuylkill at Bartram's Garden, with kayaks and rowboats, staff instruction and no sign-up needed. Open to all ages and skill levels, with minors accompanied by an adult.
records.what_you_do: Come to a Saturday session to paddle or row, or bring your own non-motorized boat. Volunteers (18 and up) can work shifts at the boathouse, but volunteer applications are closed until next season.

schedule.text: Free boating on Saturdays from 3 to 7 pm until August 29, 2026, then Saturdays from 10 am to 2 pm from September 12 to 26, 2026. No boating on some dates, and weather or river conditions can cancel.

first_step.how: Walk in during a Saturday boating session. No sign-up or past experience is needed, and minors need an adult.
first_step.basis: Staff provide the boats, gear and instruction, and the page says no experience or registration is needed.

records.notes: The riverprogram email is for community groups from Southwest Philadelphia or Grays Ferry, and the page says group rentals are not offered. The September 2026 dates are the newest evidence. The posting month is not shown. Volunteer shifts run May to October with a 3-hour orientation, and applications reopen next season. The Bartram's Garden fishing program is not part of this record.

records.name: Philadelphia Canoe Club
records.summary: A paddling club founded in 1905 at 4900 Ridge Avenue. It offers lessons in kayak, canoe and paddleboard, and its trips and events are open to the public without a membership.
records.what_you_do: Take a lesson in recreational kayak, stand up paddleboard, flatwater or whitewater canoe, or whitewater kayak. You can join a club trip, a pool session or a fall work day.

schedule.text: Fall 2026 and early 2027 events are posted, including a fall work day on October 10, 2026, a monthly club meeting on October 19, 2026 and a members banquet in January 2027. Lesson dates are not shown.

cost.text: Not shown on the home page

first_step.how: Email the club or join its mailing list. Club trips do not need a membership.
first_step.basis: Trips and training are open to the public without membership, but lesson dates and prices are not shown.

records.notes: A guessed lessons page returned 404, so the lesson list comes from the home page only. The club says it is a Paddle America club of the American Canoe Association. The events list names an organization by its initials (FOW), which is listed in leads_only. No phone number is published.

records.name: Philadelphia Dragon Boat Association
records.summary: A dragon boat club that practices on the Schuylkill at its dock near MLK Drive and Black Street. It holds several practices a week in season and plans rookie practices for newcomers in 2026.
records.what_you_do: Paddle with a team in practices from April to September, or join the planned rookie practices, where loaner paddles, seat pads and life jackets are provided.

schedule.text: Season runs April to September. Practices are Tuesday to Thursday 5:45 am to 6:45 am, Saturday usually at 9 am and Sunday at 5:30 pm, with Friday sometimes. Planned 2026 rookie practices start in mid-June, once a week to begin, on a weeknight at about 6 pm (day and time still to be set).

locations.label: Philadelphia Dragon Boat dock, near MLK Drive and Black Street

first_step.how: Fill in the interest form on the recruiting page (the club says it replies within 72 hours), or call the first-timer number to ask about rookie practices.
first_step.basis: Rookie practices are described as less intense and focused on technique, with equipment provided, and newcomers can ask in through a form.

records.notes: The recruiting page says rookie practices are planned, with the best time to join in the spring of even-numbered years, but it gives no firm start date. The phone line is for first-time visitors, to leave a message. The page names a club officer as contact, which is not recorded here. Other dragon boat leads are in leads_only.

records.name: Seaport Boat Shop at the Independence Seaport Museum
records.summary: The boat shop at the Independence Seaport Museum, where volunteers work beside master boat builders on the upkeep, restoration and building of traditional boats.
records.what_you_do: Help master boat builders with traditional vessels, from upkeep to restoration and new builds. Volunteers need a volunteer application and background clearances before the first day.

schedule.text: Boat shop volunteer roles are listed for weekdays and weekends, year round. Shifts are set through the volunteer information center once a person is accepted.

locations.label: Independence Seaport Museum, 211 S. Columbus Blvd

cost.text: The page says the required background checks are free to get online

first_step.how: Applications are closed for now because the museum says volunteer numbers are at capacity. Check the volunteer page later. Accepted volunteers need a Pennsylvania background check and a child abuse clearance before the first day.
first_step.basis: Applications are closed, and the way in is an application plus clearances.

records.notes: The phone number is the general museum line, since no volunteer email is published. The museum's boat shop page at a guessed address returned 404. The volunteer page also lists docents, the Olympia and Becuna ship crews and the research center, which are not in this record. Older materials call the shop Workshop on the Water, but that name was not confirmed on a page read here. The shipwright apprenticeship is paid, not volunteer, so it is excluded.

notes: Searches: all 3 used, so the search budget ran out before sailing clubs, Delaware River community boating and regatta volunteer programs were searched. No Schuylkill Navy regatta volunteer program was found (boathouserow.org/volunteer returned 404). Fetches: about 50. The Schuylkill Navy list (boathouserow.org/about) names 18 member clubs, 12 full and 6 associate. Each is either a record, an out_of_area verdict, blocked or in leads_only. The Schuylkill Navy itself is a governing body, not a group anyone joins, so it has no record. Several guessed page paths returned 404 (for example the Seaport boat shop page, the canoe club lessons page and the dragon boat training page variant), so those facts come from pages that did load. Unconfirmed leads from search summaries, with no URL checked: Discovery Pathways (nonprofit that has trained young Philadelphians in dragon boat since 2022), Schuylkill Paddlers (association of four Philadelphia dragon boat teams that built a shared dock on the river), and the Philadelphia Ship Model Society (has volunteered at the Seaport's Ship Shack for over ten years). The Independence Dragon Boat Regatta is a June event on Kelly Drive, not a group, so it has no record. Several status calls rest on working sites with no dated items, and those are marked probably_active with low or medium confidence. Copyright footers were not counted as evidence.
